chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, from Sajjada al-Abid (the Prostrating Worshipper), whose name is al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Uthman, from Musa ibn Bakr, who said: Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

There is no banquet (walimah) except in five situations: a wedding, childbirth, circumcision, a man buying a house, and returning from Mecca. As for the wedding, it is marriage; the childbirth is giving birth to a child; the circumcision is the cutting of the foreskin; the buying of a house is when a man purchases a home; and the returning is when one comes back from Mecca.

key_terms.خُرْس: Childbirth (literally deafness, referring to the mother's temporary loss of hearing)

ai.seo_question: What are the five occasions for hosting a walimah (banquet) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith in *Al-Khisal*, establishing a prophetic framework that restricts celebratory feasts to specific milestones to prevent extravagance and maintain social modesty. The five occasions—marriage, postpartum celebration, circumcision, home acquisition, and return from pilgrimage—highlight key life transitions where communal sharing of food strengthens social bonds within the Shia tradition.
